gloss: to make repeated efforts; to refine through trial and error

definitions.gloss: to make repeated efforts; to keep devising improvements; to refine through trial and error
definitions.explanation: To continue working on something by trying different approaches and making incremental improvements. Emphasizes persistent, creative effort over time rather than a single attempt.

examples.japanese: {工夫|くふう}を{重|かさ}ねて、ようやく{完成|かんせい}した。
examples.english: After repeated efforts, it was finally completed.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}も{工夫|くふう}を{重|かさ}ねた{結果|けっか}、{売上|うりあげ}が{伸|の}びた。
examples.english: As a result of making improvements again and again, sales increased.

examples.japanese: {味|あじ}に{満足|まんぞく}できず、{工夫|くふう}を{重|かさ}ねて{今|いま}のレシピにたどり{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: I wasn't satisfied with the taste, so I kept refining the recipe until I arrived at the current one.

notes:
Combines {工夫|くふう} (ingenuity; creative effort) with {重|かさ}ねる (to pile up; to repeat). The expression highlights the iterative nature of improvement — not just trying once but building on each attempt. It carries a positive connotation of diligence and craftsmanship.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {工夫|くふう}を{重|かさ}ねて{完成|かんせい}する: to complete through repeated effort
- {長年|ながねん}{工夫|くふう}を{重|かさ}ねる: to refine over many years
- {試行錯誤|しこうさくご}を{重|かさ}ねる: to repeat trial and error (related pattern)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {努力|どりょく}を{重|かさ}ねる: to make repeated efforts — more general; {工夫|くふう}を{重|かさ}ねる emphasizes creative problem-solving
- {改良|かいりょう}を{重|かさ}ねる: to make repeated improvements — focuses on the result (improvement) rather than the process (ingenuity)
- {試行錯誤|しこうさくご}: trial and error — describes the method but without the positive connotation of steady progress
